skill.name: python-pro
skill.description: Guides modern Python 3.12+ development with async patterns, typing, testing, performance tuning, FastAPI, uv, ruff, Pydantic, and production practices.
skill.summary: Expert guidance for modern Python architecture, tooling, testing, and performance work.
skill.author: sickn33

finding_verdicts.reason: The snippet is documentation text about Python context managers and the inline `with` keyword, not Ruby or shell execution. No executable code or command invocation exists at that location.

content.value_statement: Python teams need current guidance for reliable services, tools, and data workflows. This skill applies modern Python patterns, testing, typing, and performance practices.
actual_capabilities: Advises on Python 3.12+ language features and type hints.
Designs async workflows with asyncio, aiohttp, and Trio concepts.
Recommends uv, ruff, mypy, pyright, pytest, and pyproject workflows.
Guides FastAPI, Django, Flask, SQLAlchemy, and Pydantic application patterns.
Supports profiling, caching, memory tuning, and data pipeline optimization.
Covers Docker, CI/CD, monitoring, and deployment practices for Python services.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated code, but does not run benchmarks itself.
Recommendations depend on the project context supplied by the user.
It may need version details for framework-specific advice.
It is focused on Python, not full-stack non-Python architecture.

use_cases.title: Modernize A Service
use_cases.description: Upgrade a Python service with uv, ruff, typing, tests, and deployment practices.

use_cases.title: Review Async Design
use_cases.description: Assess concurrency choices, I/O boundaries, cancellation behavior, and performance tradeoffs before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Tooling
use_cases.description: Set up project structure, CI checks, packaging, observability, and security practices for maintainable releases.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up A Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a modern Python project plan using uv, ruff, mypy, pytest, and pyproject.toml. Include first commands and checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python module for typing, readability, errors, tests, and current best practices. Prioritize actionable fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design An API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a FastAPI service for this use case. Include validation, dependency injection, async database access, tests, and deployment notes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize A Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this data pipeline for CPU, memory, I/O, and concurrency bottlenecks. Propose profiling steps and prioritized optimizations.

output_examples.output: Assessment covering dependency migration to uv, ruff linting, type coverage, test gaps, Pydantic validation, and deployment risks.
A profiling plan, concurrency model, cancellation strategy, memory checks, and benchmark targets before implementation changes.
Endpoint structure, request validation, dependency boundaries, database session handling, test plan, and production readiness checklist.

best_practices: Share runtime versions, package constraints, and deployment targets before asking for architecture advice.
Ask for tests, typing, and error handling with each implementation request.
Use profiling data or realistic workload descriptions for performance work.
anti_patterns: Requesting broad rewrites without project goals, constraints, or failure modes.
Mixing several frameworks in one prompt without defining ownership boundaries.
Treating generated code as production-ready before tests, security review, and profiling.

faq.question: Does this skill run Python code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and generated content unless the host tool executes commands separately.

faq.question: Which Python versions does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Python 3.12+ and modern ecosystem practices from 2024 and 2025.

faq.question: Can it help migrate to uv?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline dependency migration, project configuration, lock file handling, and CI updates.

faq.question: Does it support FastAPI and Django?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers FastAPI, Django, Flask, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, authentication, and production patterns.

faq.question: Can it optimize performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest profiling, async design, caching, memory tuning, and benchmark plans.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: It can help beginners, but it is strongest for intermediate and advanced Python development tasks.
